THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE MOHAMMAD NAWAZ  ORAL ORDER Criminal Petition No.8814/2021 arises out of Crime No.27/2020 of Ashoknagar Police Station,
Bengaluru city, registered for offences punishable under Section 448, 323, 324, 384, 506, 504 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.

Criminal Petition No.6344/2021 arises out of Crime No.347/2019 of Ashoknagar Police Station,
NC: 2025:KHC:9462 Bengaluru city, registered for offences punishable under Section 498A, 323,
506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
3. Both the cases came to be registered on a complaint lodged by respondent No.2 - wife of the petitioner against the petitioner and two others.
Charge sheet is filed in both the cases against petitioner alone.
4. It is averred by respondent No.2 that her marriage with the petitioner took place on 19.01.2006 as per Hindu customs and from the wedlock they have two daughters.

Their relationship got strained and she was subjected to cruelty by the petitioner etc.,
5.

The learned counsel for petitioner has filed certified copy of the memorandum of the settlement entered between the petitioner and respondent No.2 before the family Court at Bengaluru in M.C.No.1246/2020.
It is submitted that in view of the settlement entered between the parties, their marriage has been dissolved.

"In view of the settlement, the respondent has agreed to co-operate in closing /
quashing Criminal Petition No.8814/2021 in C.C.No.53146/2021 and Criminal Petition No.6344/2021 in C.C.No.54036/2020 pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru."

7. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Panjab, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303 has held that the inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised to achieve either of twin objects namely (i) to prevent abuse of the process of any court, (ii) to do real,
complete and substantial justice.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In B.S. Joshi and others v. State of Haryana and another, reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, it becomes the duty of the Court to encourage genuine settlements of matrimonial disputes and in exercise of inherent powers, High Court can quash NC:
2025:KHC:9462 criminal proceedings and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 of the Code.

entities.text: B.S. Joshi and others v. State of Haryana and another, reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. It is well settled that the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character,
particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire dispute amongst themselves.

10. In view of the settlement taken place between the parties before the family Court, and the respondent No.2 / de-facto complainant having agreed to quash the proceedings, no purpose will be served in keeping the proceedings pending before the trial Court.

Hence, the following;
ORDER i) The criminal petitions are allowed.
ii) The entire proceedings in C.C.No.54036/2020 and C.C.No.53146/2021 pending on the file of NC:
2025:KHC:9462 XXIX Addl.
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court at Mayohall, Bengaluru City are hereby quashed.
